summary: Alert evaluation suppressed when trace-anchor URLs contain unescaped characters (pipe, slash)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports that several alert notifications did not fire for a high-severity error alert that is anchored to trace links. The anchor matching step in alert evaluation fails when trace link IDs contain unescaped characters (examples: pipe '|' or raw slashes) or are double-encoded in the trace link parameter.

Impact:
- Missed P1 alerts for BrightCart for ~2.5 hours on 2026-03-09 in us-east.
- Customers relying on trace-anchored alerts (click-to-trace) see no alert and cannot link to the trace from the notification.
- Affects any alert using trace_anchor() in the console when anchor contains characters like '|' or a pre-encoded '%2F'.

Environment:
- Prod: us-east region, console v3.12.1 evaluation engine, anchor-normalizer service v1.8.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create an alert with a condition that auto-links to a trace using trace_anchor(trace_id) in the notification template.
2) Trigger a trace with an ID that contains a pipe character (generated by internal tracing library): e.g., trace_id = "abc|def". The console stores/links traces as trace_id URL param encoded: trace_id=abc%7Cdef.
3) Observe alert eval logs and notification output.
4) Re-run with a trace id containing a literal slash or a pre-encoded slash (%2F) in the URL param.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Alert eval logs show: "anchor_lookup: returned 0 rows for key 'abc%7Cdef'" while trace index contains row for key 'abc|def'.
- Anchor-normalizer service logs include: "WARN: unexpected-percent-encoding: '%25' found in anchor-string'" when double-encoded values are passed.
- Notifications were not emitted; traces are visible in console but not linked from alerts.

Investigation notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: mismatch between how trace anchors are stored/indexed (raw/unescaped) and how alert-eval pipeline queries them (URL-encoded or double-encoded). The anchor-normalizer attempts to canonicalize, but does not handle a mixture of raw pipes and pre-encoded sequences (e.g., incoming trace URLs from BrightCart's proxy are sometimes encoded twice).
- Reproduced locally with a test trace that contains '|' -> confirmed alert eval fails to match when the alert engine receives the encoded string.
- Quick grep through service code shows alert-eval constructs lookup keys using request.query.trace_id without a final decode pass. Unit tests for anchor_normalizer cover simple encodings but not double-encoded or pipe-containing IDs.
- Related behavior referenced in SUP-42188 (sessionized-usage-splitting) and SUP-246381 (alert-links-drop-on-ad-hoc-query-rewrite) but root cause differs: this is an encoding normalization mismatch in alert path.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Short term (workaround): add a deterministic decode/normalize step in alert-eval plumbing that attempts 1x decode and fallback 2x decode before lookup. Document and release as a hotfix to console v3.12.2.
- Medium term: add unit/integration tests covering pipe and double-encoded anchors and add canonicalization logic to anchor-normalizer service.
- Longer term: add a telemetry metric for anchor lookup miss-rate and an alert when miss-rate > 0.5% for 15m.
workaround: Support provided a temporary workaround: BrightCart updated their webhook to send raw trace IDs (no double-encoding) and support created a per-organization alert template that strips percent-encoding before calling trace_anchor(). For customers that cannot change webhook behavior, we deployed a hotfix (console edge) that attempts a second decode before lookup. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4321
investigation: SRE reproduction steps, logs, and test cases created. Local repro confirmed that alert-eval fails when lookup key is encoded (abc%7Cdef) while index contains abc|def. Anchor-normalizer currently applies single url-decode; needs fallback to handle double-encoded strings and to treat '|' as a valid stored key. Traces ingestion code historically retained raw id; newer proxies perform encoding which led to mismatch.

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Investigating. Found anchor_lookup misses in alert-eval logs for the same time window. Repro steps captured and shared with eng. Tagged #support and #sre in Slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01234567/p1678530000000

2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Eng - Console): Confirmed code path where alert-eval reads request.query without decode. Will prioritize small decoder fallback and add unit tests. Assigning PR to console team.
2026-03-12 BrightCart (Customer) via email: We can temporarily change our webhook payload if that speeds up resolution. Please advise recommended format.

2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Recommended payload: send unencoded trace_id or ensure single percent-encoding (do not double-encode). SRE to deploy hotfix to edge for org=brightcart for immediate mitigation.

2026-03-13 Priya Nair (Eng - Console): Hotfix PR opened and merged to edge branch (see PR link). Plan to include in console v3.12.2 patch release. Monitoring anchor-miss metrics for BrightCart; so far 0 misses after hotfix on edge.
2026-03-13 Maya Chen (Support): Marking as In Progress. Will follow up after GA patch release and confirm with BrightCart that alerts resume normally.
